label: dgx-spark-full-capability-map
context:
Deep discussion about NVIDIA DGX Spark ($3,999) for Danny's specific use case. Danny is a 3rd-year med student (wrapping Step 1, starting clinicals end of May 2026) → future psychiatrist. Also runs Hermes Agent with distillation/Cortex and is building SOMA (3D anatomy viewer).

KEY DECISIONS MADE:
- Danny is financing the DGX Spark, treating it as long-term investment
- Primary motivation: zero API costs + HIPAA compliance for clinical apps + Hermes training loop
- NOT replacing MacBook — Spark is inference server, MacBook is dev machine
- Setup: Spark on desk alongside MacBook, MacBook USB-C to monitor, Spark connected via WiFi only
- Monitor HDMI to Spark only for initial setup/debug, 95% of time on MacBook input

COMPLETE CAPABILITY MAP BUILT (11 categories):
1. INFERENCE ENGINE: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B BF16 (40-50 tok/s), FP8 (64 tok/s), hybrid INT4+FP8 (100+ tok/s), Qwen3.5-122B-A10B NVFP4 (15-20 tok/s), Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B — all co-hostable
2. CLINICAL COMPANION: Note generator (60-90 min/day saved), pre-rounding briefs (45-60 min), drug checker (15-30 min), attending prep (25-45 min), discharge summaries (30-45 min), Anki generator (1-2 hrs/week), weekly learning report, shelf gap tracker
3. HERMES TRAINING GYM: Close the loop — Cortex 8,886 nodes → LoRA fine-tuning → model actually improves (not just tip injection). Automated nightly training. Multiple LoRA adapters. Expert specialization research.
4. RAG KNOWLEDGE BASE: DSM-5-TR, Stahl's, Kaplan & Sadock's, APA Guidelines, First Aid, UWorld, drug databases, de-identified case logs, attending patterns, Cortex data, research papers, bilingual terms
5. APP BACKEND: SOMA Clinical AI, Note Automator, Drug Checker, Case Log Dashboard, Attending Prep Bot, Anki Generator, UWorld Companion, NBME Tracker, MedCalc, bilingual terms
6. IMAGE + VISION: ComfyUI image generation (Anki/SOMA illustrations), Qwen3.6 vision (histology/pathology/radiology), medical image analysis
7. SOFTWARE DEV ASSISTANT: Local coding (SWE-bench 73.4), code review, debugging, documentation — not GLM-5.1 level but fine for 80% of work
8. MODEL EVOLUTION: Qwen3.7/3.8/4.0 drop-in upgrades, LoRA versions, model merging (dense models only, MoE merging still janky), 2nd Spark clustering path
9. RESEARCH + CAREER: PsychiatryBench evaluation paper (first-author), clinical AI portfolio, MoE expert analysis, SOMA with AI brain
10. INFRASTRUCTURE: Postgres/Cortex, Qdrant, Ollama fallback, Docker Compose, LiteLLM router, monitoring, automated backups, SSH gateway
11. FUTURE UNKNOWN: HIGGS/TurboQuant just merged into vLLM (Apr 16, today) = 6x KV cache compression = 4-6 concurrent sessions instead of 1-2. Free upgrade pattern.

HONEST ASSESSMENTS GIVEN:
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is NOT as smart as GLM-5.1 (754B model). Gap is real: ~14 points on Intelligence Index.
- Future Qwens will narrow the gap but timing uncertain (maybe Q3-Q4 2026 for Qwen3.7)
- Spark is NOT a dev workstation — it's an inference appliance. MacBook still needed for all coding.
- Model merging works for dense models but NOT well for MoE (MergeKit doesn't natively support MoE routing gates)
- LoRA provides 90-95% of full fine-tuning performance, measurable domain improvement

SPARK ALTERNATIVES ANALYZED (all have dealbreakers):
- Mac Studio M3/M4 Ultra: More bandwidth (819 GB/s) but NO CUDA, NO vLLM, NO RDMA clustering, Metal-only
- AMD Strix Halo (Framework Desktop): Half the price ($2,348) but ROCm 5x slower at prefill, broken vLLM, no RDMA
- Multi-GPU desktop: Faster decode but 72GB ceiling (35B BF16 barely fits), no upgrade path
- DGX Spark is the ONLY product with 128GB unified + CUDA + RDMA + fine-tuning ecosystem

FINANCIAL ANALYSIS:
- Z.AI savings: $180/mo = $2,160/year (pays ~40% of financing)
- Time saved: ~2 hrs/day = 480 hrs/year
- Career ROI: first-author PsychiatryBench paper = unique residency application
